Industry News: Newcastle scrape past Millwall to extend Jaissle’s unbeaten start

📅 08 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4824 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.
  • This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.
  • He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Joe Willock’s deft finish ensured Newcastle United survived a tough test against Millwall to keep their excellent run in the Carabao Cup intact.

This competition had been fruitful for Newcastle under former manager Eddie Howe and although this match was hard work – as well as hard to watch at times – his successor Matthias Jaissle guided them through a difficult trip to south-east London.

He called it “job done,” and that was pretty much all it was. “We needed patience on one hand, but also to be passionate and tough. We had the chance [to score] and took it,” he noted.

Newcastle have reached the semi-finals of this competition three times in the last four years, but struggled to get any sort of tempo going against their Championship opponents.

You could argue the winning goal came against the run of play late in the second half, moments after Millwall substitute Taïryk Arconte had smashed a low shot against the post.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

Recent findings suggest that given they were missing 13 players because of injury, this was a brave display from Alex Neil’s side. They frustrated Newcastle for more than an hour, nullifying their attack, to the point where Jaissle’s team looked as though they had run out of ideas.

According to recent reports, that was until Lewis Hall combined with Matias Fernandez-Pardo down the left and his drilled cross found Willock who cleverly used the angle to pass the ball into the net. Willock has been rejuvenated under Jaissle. He looked certain to be sold this summer but is now starting regularly under a upcoming manager in the number 10 role his system demands. It has been a nice redemption arc for the former Arsenal academy graduate.

Moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

Sources indicate that the victory is all that matters and extends Jaissle’s unbeaten start to five games. Given he arrived just three weeks before the start of the season, that deserves praise even if it is obvious there is a lot of work to be done to improve their offensive play.

Recent findings suggest that playing in their lilac, or should that be Parma-violet, third kit for the first time, Newcastle looked off colour in the first half. Even though Jaissle named a strong team packed with experience of English cup ties, they struggled to overpower Millwall.

There were a few half-chances as Willock forced a save and Jacob Murphy fired over. There was a header missed from a corner by Sven Botman, which should have hit the target and Yoane Wissa also mistimed his jump after finding space for another header.

Millwall’s two centre-backs, Jake Cooper and Caleb Taylor were immense, flinging themselves in the way of every shot and clearing every loose ball that came into their vicinity. Given their injuries, this was a performance full of fight and defiance from the home side.

However, there was also an absence of quality in the final third from Newcastle, the same lack of cohesion and incision that was apparent at home to Bournemouth last weekend and in the first half away at Tottenham Hotspur.

It meant Millwall were happy to play for set-pieces close to the Newcastle box and Taylor got in front of his marker, flashing a header wide of the post.

That lacklustre first half meant Jaissle’s side had mustered just five shots on target in five halves of football since the 3-2 win over West Bromwich Albion in the previous round of the Carabao Cup.

Millwall started the second period like a side sensing Newcastle were vulnerable. A thunderbolt from Jenson Metcalfe, after the visitors had struggled to clear two crosses, almost gave them a spectacular lead.

Newcastle saw lots of the ball. Millwall were happy enough to let them have it given how little they were hurting them.

So much of Newcastle’s play was slow and cumbersome. Their set-piece delivery was also largely inept.

Neil’s side retained a threat and came so close to taking the lead when, not for the first time, a long ball forward caught the Newcastle defence out of shape and Tino Livramento’s mistake allowed Arconte to run clear and hit the post from a tight angle.

In a recent development, well in, @Joewillock! 💪 pic.twitter.com/5a8G7lzD3H.

Speaking after the game, Millwall manager Alex Neil remarked: “I’m very proud, I don’t think we deserved to lose that game.

“We had some good moments, and we got done by a bit of sucker punch at the end. But I’m very proud of the lads.”.

As for their injury problems, he added: “I didn’t bring the teenagers on as a token gesture, I need to keep the first-team players fit. We’re really at bare bones.

But we beat Bolton at the weekend, got a couple of defeats before that but we started the season really well and once we get everybody back, we’ll be in good shape.”.

With the first of the 16 teams through tonight, the draw won’t take place until most of the teams have played next week.

In a recent development, the draw will be shown on Sky Sports on Wednesday 16th Sept, after Manchester United play Brighton. Man City vs Norwich will be the only game outstanding then.

The third round had to be spread over two weeks as the nine Premier League sides in UEFA competitions entered the tournament in this round, as the same time as their Champions League and Europa League fixtures began. To avoid clubs facing clashes, the EFL split the fixtures across the two gameweeks.

Still got some more post-match to come for you, but we’ve got scores from all our matches tonight now:.

Crystal Palace 3-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-3 Bradford City.

From the Champions League, Man City held out against Porto to win 2-0.

“I think we had a lot of chances in the first half, and we went in a half-time saying we need to  take our chances, so I’m glad we came out in the second half and we did,” said Willock after the match.

“100% [the competition is vital], we’ve won it before so it’s very important to us, but every game is important to us. Especially with a fresh coach and a lot of new players, we wanted to start the new season well. I think we started really well and we need to continue and this was a substantial game in keeping that momentum.”.

"We mentioned at half-time we NEED to take our chances"Lewis Hall and Joe Willock react to Newcastle's win over Millwall 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/NDF3laD8nT.

Take a look at the match-winner from Joe Willock:.

Recent findings suggest that moments after Millwall hit the post, Joe Willock strikes to put Newcastle in front! ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/rSB8yV6NRO.

The goal came minutes after Millwall were inches away from taking the lead themselves, as Arconte was denied by the post:.

"Livramento had a NIGHTMARE, he's so lucky" 😨Millwall were INCHES away from taking the lead against Newcastle 🤏 pic.twitter.com/X26aiTL432.

We’ll be bringing you more from the post-match now.

Joe Willock has done enough for Newcastle to reach the fourth round and keep the travelling fans singing all the way back to the North-East.

It won’t go down in history as the greatest Carabao fixture, but Newcastle found a way to keep their momentum going and give Matthias Jaissle a win on his cup debut.

Newcastle aren’t taking any risks as Hornicek sends the ball long, and the players keep looking to send the ball down-field.

It has been revealed that seconds to go now. Marschall sends it long for one last effort, but it is cleared out of the box...

Willock has come off now for Newcastle’s own teenager, Sean Steur. A few more minutes and the man now on the bench with have done enough to send his side through to the next round.

We’re into the final minutes as Millwall are throwing everything at this.

Millwall are not out of this yet, as Neghli comes down the left side, twisting his way into the box past his defender – but having done the hard work, his shot flashes low across goal.

Some more changes, as Ramsey comes off for Newcastle, replaced by Lewis Miley.

A double change for the hosts as Dykes and Kelly come off for Regan Monty and Alfie Massey – the former just 15 years old.

Seconds later, another teenager takes to the pitch for Millwall as Osei-Tutu is replaced by 17-year-old Tristan Parkes.

Newcastle almost have another! From the sublime to the ridiculous, as Willock makes another run, this time down the left, and passes the ball onto the edge of the box where Elanga meets it in space. He lets it run, before taking his shot, but it is straight to Marschall.

Finally Newcastle have their breakthrough! They punish Millwall as Fernandez-Pardo feeds Hall on the left, who cuts inside and slips the ball across goal, finding Willock to redirect the ball to slot it home.

You can hear the travelling fans now!

Industry observers note that marschall releases Arconte with a long ball and he turns Livramento to find huge amounts of space on the right side. He races into the box and takes a shot from close range, aiming for his near post, but is denied by the woodwork and the rebound hits the seated Hornicek. The keeper is lucky to not concede an own goal, as the ball bounces up and over his leg.

Issoufou again racing down the right side, before cutting inside and taking a shot with his left foot. Hall, who has been so crucial in the Newcastle attack, throws himself at the shot, and it flies high for Hornicek to collect.

Replays show that González, who Millwall players claimed had handled the ball earlier, leant down to clear with his shoulder.

Issoufou sends a great ball in for Millwall from the right side, but it is cleared by a Newcastle player, accompanied by cries for handball.

The game is opening up now as Newcastle make a run of their own, with Willock creating an opening for Elanga to take the ball to the edge of the box, before Taylor slides in to block his shot.

Sources indicate that millwall could absolutely win this with a smash-and-grab with less than 20 minutes to go. They are pushing for it but are lacking some attacking quality to finish the job.

From six shots they’ve had two on target, compared to Newcastle’s three on target from 20.

Fernandez-Pardo gets his first look at the ball, making a very quick run down across the centre of the field to the left side, but Osei-Tutu stays with him and takes him all the way to the back line before giving up a corner.

Elanga takes the corner, punched away by the keeper but no one goes to finish the job and Newcastle get another corner.

Metcalfe, who had his red card overturned this week, is the first player to go in the book for a mistimed challenge on Ramsey.

Just a reminder that there is no extra time, so if we’re all square after 90 minutes, it’s straight to a penalty shoot-out.

Willock gets the ball on the edge of the area and passes it on a quick turn to Barnes just inside the box, but there was not much on his shot and Marschall collects easily.

In a recent development, double change now for Newcastle as Wissa and Murphy come off, replaced by Elanga and Fernandez-Pardo as Jaissle looks for pace. Schar is handed the armband.

Free kick for Newcastle, right on the corner of the box. Murphy takes, but it hits the wall 10 feet away, and bounces straight back to him. His cross into the box is headed out, and for all the opportunities Newcastle have created, they are yet to find the breakthrough.

We’ve also had a double change for Millwall as Esse and Lovelace have come off, replaced by Issoufou and Arconte.

What colour would you describe this Newcastle away shirt? They look like the sweets Purple Violet to me. Although would you call it an all Lilac number?

It’s the first time they have worn their third kit. Not sure whether I like it or not. Shame The Den isn’t a sell out although I’m told tickets were priced at £31 and Millwall have a lot of injuries too.

Recent findings suggest that newcastle get another corner after a run from Willock. The delivery from Hall creates a good amount of confusion in the box and Marschall isn’t sure whether to stay on his line or come out to punch it away. From within the bodies, Wissa tries to get a shot off from close range but it bounces and the keeper easily collects.

González commits another foul, pulling down Esse, to give Millwall another free kick from 40 yards out.

The ball meets Taylor at the back post, but he meets it in the air and can’t quite direct it either into goal or back into the six-yard box, so it goes out for a Newcastle goal kick.

Another half chance for Millwall as Dykes feeds Kelly on the right side, who runs into the box and gets caught between passing the ball in and taking the shot, with the ball going high over the box.

Another great challenge from Osei-Tutu as Willock makes a run into the box, but is brought down by a well-timed tackle from the right-back.

The corner from Hall is better, but headed out and cleared.

Barnes again with space on the left side and he sends a ball fizzing low across the box to the far post but Neghli is able to lean on Murphy to stop him making contact.

Scramble for Newcastle as the ball is sent by Dykes to Neghli free at the far post, who puts the ball into a very dangerous area just in front of goal and everyone jumps on. Newcastle get to it first, managing to clear it from the goal mouth. It is cleared outside the box and it bounces to unmarked Metcalfe, who takes a thunderous shot, putting his laces through the ball but he is unable to keep it down and it goes over the bar.

Promising restart for the home side.

Despite Alex Neil’s premonitions, no changes for Millwall at the break.

Right-back change for Newcastle, as Dedic comes off and Tino Livramento comes on.

The earlier kick-offs of the Carabao third round have just started their second periods, but here are the latest scores:.

Crystal Palace 1-0 Middlesbrough.

Leyton Orient 1-1 Bradford City.

Aston Villa won their opening Champions League fixture 3-2 against Club Brugge, while Man City are still goalless against Porto, which you can follow with our live blog here.

And that’s the last action of the half, as just one minute was added on and that was taken up by Newcastle’s corner.

Nothing separates the two sides at the half, thought the visitors have dominated in terms of possession and chances.

Sources indicate that millwall have held fast and will be happy to be finishing the half level. We may see some changes from them after the break.

It has been revealed that the game is opening up before half-time, and Newcastle go again with Hall and Barnes. Osei-Tutu does well to wait before going in to block Barnes’s shot and send the ball behind for another Newcastle corner.

Industry observers note that the delivery is once again poor, but Schar is pulled down inside the box by Taylor and is furious that nothing was given. There’s no VAR so there’s no review to consider – but looking at replays, Millwall were very lucky to get away with that foul.

Cooper makes a perfect pass down the left sideline, allowing Neghli to find space and forcing Newcastle to clear it away fo a Millwall corner.

The ball in is promising but Hornicek gets to it and punches it away, but the hosts keep the pressure on.

Baggott floats another ball across the box towards the right back post, but Hornicek easily collects the ball as Neghli can’t quite connect.

Newcastle moving the ball well again across midfield and it comes to Schar, who runs into space and gets a low shot away, around 40 yards out. It  takes a slight deflection on its way, going just wide of the post.

González is not having his best night and makes a silly foul against Dykes on the sideline, giving the hosts another set piece. The swinging ball in is not nearly as good as last time, and only reaches the first man, Newcastle’s Ramsey.

In a recent development, millwall get a free kick, and the delivery is good, allowing Taylor to connect on the header inside the box. He beats Hornicek but the header rolls just wide of the post, to the groans of the home fans.

Hall goes short with the corner and Dedic has lots of time to cross the ball in from the right. It’s headed away but Millwall can’t break on the counter.

That sums up the game pretty well: not much finishing quality from Newcastle but Millwall not creating much from their limited spells of possession.

According to recent reports, newcastle pushing again. Another ball pulled back by Barnes finds Ramsey at the top of the box, and his ball in connects with Wissa. Newcastle’s captain can’t head it in the right direction though and Millwall survive again.

The spell of pressure results in another corner for the visitors – and now we’re getting some pushing in the six-yard box.

It has been revealed that I think Millwall have done well. They have limited Newcastle to half chances and the odd set piece threat. They have made things really difficult for the visitors, crowding them out of space on the edge of the area.

When the home side have advanced up the pitch the Newcastle defence has not looked particularly secure.

As we reach the half-hour mark, Newcastle have 10 shots to Millwall’s one, though they sit one apiece on shots on target.

Esse gets caught on his heels as Hall pulls a long ball back on the left, and in the crowd at the top of the box Willock takes a shot, pulling it wide – cheers from the home crowd again.

First piece of good attacking play from Millwall as Neghli and Baggott work on the overlap. Baggott lofts a high ball to the back post, where Dykes gets a foot on it on the volley, but he can’t quite get over it and it’s easily picked up by Hornicek.

According to recent reports, barnes and Ramsey combine again down the left, with the midfielder trying to feed Barnes on his run. The pass has too much on it though, and as it runs out the back it’s met with jeers from the home fans for a goal kick.

Recent findings suggest that wissa breaks away down the centre of the field, with Barnes on his left, using him as a decoy. Wissa takes the shot though and it is blocked by a sliding defender.

Sources indicate that newcastle hit 20 minutes in with 68 per cent possession but nothing to show yet for their efforts. You feel like it will only be a matter of time though.

Another Newcastle corner, swung in well and Botman comes charging in, beating cooper to a free header. The defender heads it over the bar and holds his head in his hands. The visitors could definitely be a goal up by now.

Hall’s free-kick is met by the first man Metcalfe who heads it away to atone for his foul and Newcastle remain stymied.

Millwall will have expected Newcastle to dominate the ball but they are really pushing for an opener, especially down the left side with Barnes and Hall.

In a recent development, again, Newcastle coming down the wings, this time on the left. Esse picks the ball up but loses it and Willock picks it up and takes a shot on his right foot with good power but sends it straight at Marschall. The debut keeper parries it away and it’s cleared by a  Millwall header.

Willock comes down the left soon after and is fouled by Metcalfe to get a free kick in a good spot outside the box.

Murphy gets a shot off after Dedic picks up a long ball on the right side and crosses it back towards the middle of the field. Murphy gets on it and takes the shot inside the box off his left foot but it sails over the bar.

González gives the ball away cheaply and Metcalfe picks it up, but unable to move it forward.

Newcastle will need to make sure they don’t get complacent in defence.

Millwall having a spell of possession, the counter-attack looking like their best option but as they move down the right hand side, Lovelace makes a late challenge to get the ball back and fouls Wissa.

Sources indicate that newcastle advancing, with Dedic and Ramsey moving the ball across midfield. Barnes gets the ball on the left of the box, and his ball is in knocked out and Newcastle get the first corner of the game.

Nothing comes of it as it is sent in high and long over the box.

In a recent development, fair to say both teams are settling, but Millwall try and create a chance with Lovelace, though it’s intercepted. Dykes takes a bit of a knock and is slow to get up.

Here we go in south London, and Millwall get us started.

Just a reminder of the teams starting today:.

Starting XI: Filip Marschall; Jordi Osei-Tutu, Caleb Taylor, Jake Cooper, Elkan Baggott; Lyndon Dykes, Jenson Metcalfe; Camiel Neghli, Daniel Kelly, Romain Esse; Zak Lovelace.

Substitutes: Regan Monty, Tristan Parkes, Sacha Vieira, George Beaumont, Yanis Issoufou, George Evans, Taïryk Arconte, Alfie Massey, Zak Sturge.

Starting XI: Lukás Hornícek; Lewis Hall, Fabian Schär, Amar Dedic, Sven Botman; Jacob Murphy, Nico González; Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Joe Willock; Yoane Wissa.

Substitutes: Tino Livramento, Anthony Elanga, Malick Thiaw, Nick Pope, Lewis Miley, Bazoumana Touré, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, Aladji Bamba, Sean Steur.

The teams are coming out of the tunnel, and both home and away fans in the Den are already in loud voice. Kick off on the way!

"We've tried to find the right balance" ⚖️Matthias Jaissle on his team selection for tonight's match with Millwall ⚫️ pic.twitter.com/kiRRxAgLk8.

We’re just a few minutes away from kick off in south London, but Bournemouth have scored the first goal of the third round, with Ryan Christie putting his side ahead against Lincoln.

It has been revealed that alex Neil has not minced his words over his squad’s injury crisis. His team is down 13 players, which the coach says has “definitely forced” his hand in terms of squad rotation.

Playing two matches a week in the “relentless” Championship has turned his squad selection into a “needs must scenario” and he even admitted he “may need to make a couple of changes at half-time depending on how the game goes”.

Matthias Jaissle is clearly taking this competition seriously and having started the league well, he is still trying to get the fans onside and create momentum for his team.

At the same time, Telegraph Sport have reported that Ross Wilson, the sporting director, has warned there will have to be more departures in future windows. Having lost Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães in 12 months, there will be yet be more upheaval.

You can read Luke Edwards’ full story on that here.

Sources indicate that the Premier League teams playing in European competitions enter the EFL Cup in this round, with all 16 fixtures being played over five match days. As well as tonight’s games there will be:.

Peterborough United vs Barnsley (7.45pm).

Fleetwood Town vs Sheffield United (7.45pm).

Manchester City vs Norwich City (7.30pm).

*all kick-off at 8pm, unless stated otherwise.

Newcastle have named a strong side – probably the strongest they could field when factoring in senior players needing game time – to take on Millwall in the Carabao Cup.

Jacob Ramsey impressed coming off the bench against Bournemouth last weekend and manager Matthias Jaissle refused to sanction winger Jacob Murphy’s transfer to Nottingham Forest late in the window. Both deserve a chance to impress from the start.

Veteran centre back Fabian Schar comes in for Malick Thiaw, but those are the only three changes from the side that drew with Bournemouth.

Jaissle insisted he would take the competition seriously and the teamsheet proves it, but it also raises questions about some of Newcastle’s summer recruitment.

Bazoumana Toure cost £42m but was withdrawn at half time in the win over West Brom in the previous round, which means Harvey Barnes does not get a rest. That’s a lot of money to spend on a winger who has not looked Premier League ready so far.

According to recent reports, aladji Bamba, a £30m signing from Monaco, has not started a game yet and has been an unused substitute since the opening game against Liverpool. He remains on the bench.

Even Sean Steur, who has looked good since his summer move from Ajax, cannot dislodge another more recent arrival in former Manchester City midfielder Nico González.

Having made a total of eight new signings in a much-vaunted summer rebuild, Jaissle only started three of them against Bournemouth and only two start tonight at The Den.

Early days but this was one of the main reasons Eddie Howe quit – he did not think the likes of Toure, Steur and Bamba were ready to play first team football.

The visitors have arrived in south London.

We've made it to South East London 👋 pic.twitter.com/nh8Fpa37xT.

We’re bringing you the action from the pick of tonight’s EFL Cup games but there are also four games kicking off at 7.45pm:.

Crystal Palace vs Middlesbrough.

The Champions League also returns tonight and you can follow along with both our blogs:.

Aston Villa are currently 3-1 up against Club Brugge in Belgium – follow the action here.

Manchester City will face Porto at 8.00pm – our live blog has just gone live here with the team news from both sides.

Here is how the visitors are lining up:.

Yoane Wissa takes the captain’s armband tonight, while Jacob Ramsey starts up front after scoring a late equaliser against Bournemouth on Saturday.

Your Mags at Millwall ✊ pic.twitter.com/zfnHgTlWgh.

Here is your Millwall starting XI:.

Keeper Filip Marschall is making his debut while Jensen Metcalfe is back in the squad after his red card against Bolton was overturned on appeal.

How your Lions line-up tonight 🔢 pic.twitter.com/wEp6qLIz4Y.

Welcome to tonight’s live coverage of Millwall vs Newcastle United, as the Geordies travel to south London for the third round of the Carabao Cup.

In a recent development, newcastle held off West Brom in their second-round match, with Harvey Barnes scoring two second-half goals to see his side through. It was a mighty comeback, after Isaac Price scored early to stun the crowd at St James’ Park. Bazoumana Toure equalised for Matthias Jaissle’s side just before half-time, and Barnes, his replacement in the second half, put them ahead minutes after the restart. West Brom pulled it back to 2-2 with a penalty converted by Price after Lewis Hall was deemed to have handled the ball in the box, but Barnes got his second just nine minutes from full-time and the hosts were able to see out the match to progress.

Recent findings suggest that alex Neil’s Millwall have reached round three via a 0-1 win over Cambridge United, following a penalty shoot-out in the first round to beat QPR. They come into this tie with a squad stretched thin, as they have been hit with an injury crisis a month into the latest season. Millwall have confirmed that they will be without Casper De Norre, Josh Coburn, Tristan Crama, Alfie Doughty, Mathis Servais, Ryan Leonard, Mihailo Ivanovic, Lukas Jensen and Luke Cundle.

Both sides sit seventh in their respective leagues, with Millwall on a record of three wins and two losses this season, while Newcastle remain unbeaten (two draws and a win).

Newcastle will hoping to progress smoothly in a tournament that they have recently enjoyed good form in – winners in 2025 and semi-finalists last season – and with Millwall dealing with a bare bones squad, the Championship side are the underdogs on paper going into this fixture.

But, as always, anything can happen, so let us know your score prediction in the comments and we’ll be bringing you team news soon!

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 11:20, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:20.

Real Madrid will be aiming to continue their excellent run of form when they resume their La Liga campaign against Celta Vigo on Saturday night.

Los Blancos have been victorious in each of their last eight matches in all competitions, including a 3-0 success over Valencia before the November international break.

Jose Mourinho's side are right now second in the La Liga table, three points behind the leaders Barcelona, boasting a record of 10 wins and two draws from their 12 league matches during the 2026-27 campaign.

Celta, meanwhile, have a record of two wins, seven draws and three defeats from their 12 games during the current season.

The Vigo outfit are right now 11th in the division on 13 points.

Here, Sports Mole looks at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Real Madrid and Celta ahead of their clash in the Spanish capital this weekend.

These two sides have locked horns on 139 occasions throughout history, and Real Madrid comfortably lead the head-to-head record, having won 83 times to Celta's 35, while there have also been 21 draws.

Real Madrid have netted 324 times against Celta, conceding 175, while Cristiano Ronaldo is the all-time leading goalscorer in this fixture, having scored 20 goals against the Sky Blues during his time with Los Blancos.

Unsurprisingly, Real Madrid have also dominated their La Liga meetings, winning 73 of their 120 matches, suffering 30 defeats in the process, while there have been 17 draws.

Notably, three of Celta's last four wins over Real Madrid have actually come at the Bernabeu, while they have only beaten Los Blancos once in front of their own supporters since May 2001.

Real enjoyed a 10-game winning run against Celta in La Liga between May 2014 and December 2025, when Os Celestes emerged 2-0 winners in the Spanish capital during their most recent clash at Bernabeu.

Xabi Alonso's side came into that game desperate to keep up with Barcelona in the title race, but after conceding the first goal to Williot Swedberg's brilliant flick early in the second half, frustrations grew.

Madrid left-back Fran Garcia picked up two yellow cards in around sixty seconds shortly beyond the hour mark, before Alvaro Fernandez Carreras saw a straight red for abusing the referee in stoppage time.

To make matters worse, Swedberg then added a second when he was played through by Celta legend Iago Aspas and dribbled around Thibaut Courtois before walking the ball into an empty net.

However, Real Madrid were able to gain some revenge in the reverse meeting in Vigo in March 2026, with the capital giants recording a last-gasp 2-1 in.

Celta will now be aiming to make it back-to-back wins over Real Madrid at Bernabeu.

La capolista affronta il Lecce, fermo a 10 punti; la squadra di Gasperini trova il Parma, a quota otto.

According to recent reports, lazio e Roma possono allungare a 12 giornate il loro primato congiunto di imbattibilità nel prossimo turno di Serie A. Dopo la sosta per le Nazionali, il campionato 2026-27 riprende con la dodicesima giornata, in programma dal 21 al 23 novembre 2026. Le due squadre capitoline giocheranno entrambe sabato 21 novembre.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Come riportato da Opta, Lazio e Roma sono rimaste entrambe imbattute nelle prime 11 giornate per la prima volta nella storia delle formazioni romane nella massima serie. Il risultato raggiunto prima della pausa può quindi essere migliorato nel prossimo turno: se nessuna delle due perderà, la serie condivisa salirà a 12 giornate.

Le partite delle due squadre sono concentrate nello spazio di poche ore. Alle 15 la Lazio ospiterà il Lecce all’Olimpico; alle 18 toccherà alla Roma, impegnata sul campo del Parma. Saranno questi i due incontri da cui dipenderà la possibilità di prolungare il primato congiunto.

  • By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026.

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

Daily Mail Sport's Tara Anson-Walsh and Samara Watts were at Stamford Bridge to bring you the things we learned...

Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blew the title race wide open.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson.

Devastation for Kadeisha Buchanan, who was hooked after 11 minutes by Bompastor. The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor noted.

Sources indicate that 'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'.

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.

The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match and was hooked after just 11 minutes.

Women’s football royalty Sarina Wiegman and Emma Hayes braved the chilly climes of Stamford Bridge to witness the showdown between the WSL heavyweights on Saturday afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that the freshly anointed honorary Dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes and the pair chatted warmly, with Wiegman laughing as Hayes attempted to encourage her to celebrate Chelsea's victory at full time. This is a relationship that will no doubt drop in cordiality as the sand in the hourglass ahead of next summer’s World Cup continues to run down.

Wiegman had several England players on her watching brief, not least young Lexi Potter, whose stock has risen dramatically this season. The 20-year-old put in another assured performance against the reigning champions, continuing to demonstrate her maturity in the highest stakes, which will no doubt put her in a good position ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement.

In a recent development, elsewhere, the Dutch coach will have been alarmed by the number of crunching tackles put in against her right back, Lucy Bronze, in this match. If there is one player that she will want to wrap up in cotton wool ahead of Brazil, it is the recently turned 35-year-old Bronze for her steadfast leadership and relentless athleticism.

One player looking to make an impact ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement was Aggie Beever-Jones, who has struggled this season and was left out of Sonia Bompastor’s starting line-up. An injury to Melvine Malard saw Beever-Jones gain more minutes than she would have expected, but it felt like another afternoon of deja vu for the 23-year-old forward as she failed to convert a number of chances despite finding herself in good positions.

Meanwhile, in Manchester, Ella Toone's hopes of forcing her way back into Sarina Wiegman's intends suffered another blow as the 27-year-old was once again left out of Eva Olid's starting line-up for United's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Toone watched on as fellow Lioness Maya Le Tissier opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike, and the two-time European champion will no doubt be growing increasingly concerned as Brazil draws closer.

The freshly anointed honorary dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes at the WSL showpiece at Stamford Bridge and the pair chatted warmly.

Recent findings suggest that melvine Malard’s absence raises questions about who Chelsea’s main goalscorer will be this season. The squad has lacked a clinical edge without England striker Lauren James, who is out with a hamstring injury until the international break.

According to recent reports, the French forward went off injured after 35 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury. Although she missed Chelsea’s opening games after picking up a knock in pre-season, she has been the Blues’ top scorer in the absence of Lauren James with six league goals so far.

Chelsea are averaging 24 shots per game, an unprecedented rate across a WSL campaign, but have recently struggled to convert their chances. They were held to a 0-0 draw against BK Hacken midweek in the UWCL and a 1-1 draw against Everton last weekend.

According to recent reports, malard leaving the pitch meant Chelsea struggled to find a creative spark up front. Her replacement Aggie Beever-Jones has been dealing with an ankle injury, and is still trying to find her feet with only one goal in the WSL.

Head coach Bompastor stated: ‘The frustration sometimes comes from us not being ruthless and clinical.’.

Industry observers note that A moment of magic from Malard’s French international teammate Sandy Baltimore was enough to make it 1-0 just before half time with the team’s first shot on target. However, Baltimore was substituted at half time to manage her minutes, and Chelsea were unable to capitalize on any of their chances in the second half.

Bompastor noted: ‘From the outside it seems like we have had a lot of injuries, but we have been playing every three days.’.

‘I knew coming into the game we were not as fresh as we would like to be, but that’s our environment.

‘We want to play in every competition but the players are not robots,’.

Melvine Malard’s injury could cause more problems for the Blues’ attack, as they registered just two shots on target today and scraped the three points.

Malard limped off in the first half and meant Chelsea struggled for a creative spark up front.

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box and took down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal in the 75th minute.

The Blues were mounting a rapid attack down the left hand side, with Thompson just outside the box when Yamashita missed the ball and brought her to the ground.

In a recent development, the Japanese goalkeeper was shown a straight red card and was sent off the pitch. This was City’s first red card in the WSL since November 2023, and a rare moment of madness from the usually-composed 31-year-old.

The referee allowed City three minutes to replace the Japanese goalkeeper, with Scotland’s number one Eartha Cumings coming on to replace forward Aoba Fujino.

Her first test arrived only a minute later, as Aggie Beever-Jones' right-footed shot from the resulting indirect free kick dropped dangerously, but she was saved by the crossbar.

The bigger question now is whether Yamashita's absence - which could amass to three games - will have a lasting impact on their title race.

Sources indicate that in the short-term against Chelsea, City reacted well. Andree Jeglertz stated at full time: ‘The players dealt with it in a good way, so even though we were one player down we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal. Of course it affected the game but that is not why we lost.’.

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as Manchester City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box to take down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal.

Chelsea’s win at the Bridge blows the title race wide open, as they are now just one point ahead of City at the top of the WSL table.

Bompastor’s side ended City’s unbeaten streak, and they now have 24 league goals compared to City’s 16 after 10 games.

However, with seven shots and just one on target this game, Chelsea will need to look at their attacking options as they take on Liverpool and London City Lionesses before the international break.

Bompastor noted: ‘It’s a nice feeling to be top of the table right now and to win against these top sides, but I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it’s early on in the season so many things can happen.’.

City were unable to create opportunities in front of goal, with the WSL’s all-time leading goalscorer Vivianne Miedema’s return overshadowed by Ayaka Yamashita’s nightmare in goal.

City head coach Andree Jeglertz said: ‘They managed to score on their major chance and (it was a) great finish.

'We also had some great opportunities where we didn’t manage to score, but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.’.

London City Lionesses face Arsenal tomorrow at the Emirates, and a win in north London could bring them four points behind the latest WSL leaders, and really start to make things interesting.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 11:25, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:18.
  • Seeking to end a three-game losing run in the Premier League, Manchester City welcome Fulham to the Etihad Stadium for Saturday’s lunchtime kickoff.
  • These two teams last butted heads nine months ago when three first-half goals helped the Citizens claim a comfortable 3-0 home victory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 11:25, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:18.

Seeking to end a three-game losing run in the Premier League, Manchester City welcome Fulham to the Etihad Stadium for Saturday’s lunchtime kickoff.

These two teams last butted heads nine months ago when three first-half goals helped the Citizens claim a comfortable 3-0 home victory.

Man City are just the second team in English top-flight history – after Sheffield Wednesday back in 1904-05 – to win their first seven matches of a season and then lose their next three, suffering defeat to Aston Villa, Brighton & Hove Albion and Nottingham Forest before the international break.

Liam Delap haunted his former club by scoring twice in a deserved 3-1 home victory for Forest a fortnight ago, with costly defensive mistakes and a lack of intensity proving to be key factors behind the downfall of Enzo Maresca’s side.

Only Sunderland (six) and Hull City (five) have committed more errors leading to goals in the top flight this season than Man City (four), who have slipped to third in the Premier League table and six points off the summit ahead of a crunch trip to leaders Arsenal at the Emirates at the end of this month.

The international break has given City a welcome chance to reset, and Maresca has insisted there is no reason to panic just yet, even though his side have shipped 17 goals across their last eight games in all competitions, including eight first-half goals in 10 league outings.

After losing 1-0 to Brighton in their most recent home fixture, Man City are in danger of suffering back-to-back league defeats at the Etihad for the first time since May 2021, while they have not lost successive home games without scoring since December 2008.

However, Man City should be confident of success on Saturday, as they have won each of their last 20 meetings with Fulham across all competitions, including 17 straight victories in the Premier League – the longest winning run against the same opponent in English football history.

Fulham extended their unbeaten run in the Premier League to four matches (W2 D2) after coming from behind to rescue a point in a 1-1 draw with Newcastle United at Craven Cottage before the international break.

Jacob Murphy thought he had scored the winner with a superb curling strike 10 minutes from time, but Fulham restored parity just three minutes later when substitute Rodrigo Muniz stabbed home an equaliser – his first Premier League goal since the opening weekend of last season.

Head coach Alvaro Arbeloa was pleased with his side’s reaction to going a goal down late in the tight contest, and Fulham now sit 15th in the table, two points above the relegation zone and three points behind the top half.

Fulham rank third for both accurate passes per game (493.4) and touches in the opposition’s box (327), and fifth for average possession (57.7%) in the Premier League this season, yet their dominance on the ball has failed to translate into goals, with only Sunderland (eight) and Nottingham Forest (nine) finding the net fewer times than the Cottagers (10) after 10 matches.

Tricky tests against Man City, Bournemouth and Tottenham are up next for Fulham, who head into Saturday’s fixture seeking to win their first match at the Etihad since April 2009 when Clint Dempsey netted a brace in a 3-1 victory for Roy Hodgson’s side.

Manchester City Premier League form:.

Manchester City form (all competitions):.

Fulham form (all competitions):.

Man City attacker Antoine Semenyo remains sidelined with a knee injury, while Matheus Nunes (unspecified) and Abdukodir Khusanov (knock) are both "doubtful" according to Maresca.

However, Marc Guehi has taken part in training this week and should be ready to play after withdrawing from the England squad with a hip problem.

If Maresca decides against starting Guehi, this could open the door for 20-year-old Brazil international Vitor Reis to start his first PL match under the new City boss alongside captain Ruben Dias, while Josko Gvardiol is fit and ready to rival Nico O'Reilly for the left-back berth after sustaining an unspecified injury against Forest.

In a recent development, maresca has a big decision to make over whether to continue with Enzo Fernandez alongside star midfielder Elliot Anderson or recall Ayyoub Bouaddi to play in a double pivot. Rayan Cherki, meanwhile, will likely retain his place in the number 10 role.

One player certain to start is Erling Haaland, who has scored eight goals in as many games against Fulham, while he has scored 20 goals in as many matches for club and country so far this season, netting three times in two games for Norway during the international break.

As for Fulham, Tom Cairney is available for selection after recovering from a niggling knee issue, but Emile Smith Rowe (hip) and Benjamin Lecomte (Achilles) are both ruled out through injury.

Man United-linked Calvin Bassey will likely start alongside David Affengruber at centre-back, while Man City academy graduates Shea Charles and Oscar Bobb are both expected to play in midfield and on the right wing respectively.

After scoring as a substitute last time out, striker Rodrigo Muniz will be pushing to start his first PL game of the season ahead of Gonzalo Garcia, who is without a goal in each of his last nine starts since netting on the opening weekend of the season.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Lewis, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Bouaddi; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku; Haaland.

Fulham possible starting lineup:.

Leno; Castagne, Affengruber, Bassey, Robinson; Berge, Charles; Bobb, King, Iwobi; Garcia.

Maresca will demand a strong reaction from his Man City players following recent setbacks, and their exceptional historical record in this fixture firmly establishes them as the favourites to claim all three points.

While a porous Citizens backline offers encouragement to a Fulham outfit that has drawn a blank in seven of their last 12 Premier League games on the road, we expect the hosts' attacking firepower to comfortably outgun the Cottagers on this occasion.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 11:25, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:33.
  • Without a win in any competition for almost a month, under-pressure Wouter Vrancken takes his Hearts side to Dens Park this weekend to face Dundee as the Scottish Premiership returns following the international break.
  • The Dee headed into the international break in fifth place after a narrow 2-1 defeat to St Johnstone, while the Jambos suffered a third consecutive loss after being thrashed 5-2 at home by an in-form Falkirk side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Calum Burrowes | 19 Nov 2026 11:25, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 11:33.

Without a win in any competition for almost a month, under-pressure Wouter Vrancken takes his Hearts side to Dens Park this weekend to face Dundee as the Scottish Premiership returns following the international break.

The Dee headed into the international break in fifth place after a narrow 2-1 defeat to St Johnstone, while the Jambos suffered a third consecutive loss after being thrashed 5-2 at home by an in-form Falkirk side.

After a relatively quiet end to the 2025-26 season, during which Dundee neither threatened relegation nor came close to securing European football, Steven Pressley entered the newly introduced campaign hoping to take his side a step further.

Now approaching his 18th month in charge at Dens Park, Pressley has overseen five wins, two draws and five defeats in the opening 12 matches of the 2026-27 season, leaving the Dee fifth in the table and with an opportunity to leapfrog their upcoming opponents with a victory on Saturday afternoon.

Dundee won just one of their four matches leading up to the international break, a comfortable victory over bottom side Kilmarnock, while a draw against Rangers and 2-1 defeats to St Mirren and St Johnstone suggest the two-week stoppage may have come at a welcome time for Pressley's side.

A key factor behind their early-season fortunes has been their solid defensive record, with the side based on the north bank of the Firth of Tay conceding just 15 goals in their opening 12 Scottish Premiership outings, making their latest defeat all the more frustrating.

Dundee suffered an error-strewn defeat in the Tayside derby in Perth at the start of the month, losing 2-1 to St Johnstone, and will know that individual mistakes have prevented them from climbing further up the table.

Despite their inconsistent form, the Dee remain just four points behind third-placed Falkirk, with a game in hand, and will know that a victory against a depleted Hearts side this weekend could further strengthen their impressive start to the campaign.

As for the visitors, Hearts make the journey north from the Scottish capital on the back of three consecutive defeats across the Scottish League Cup, Conference League and Scottish Premiership.

Their cup run came to an end against rivals Hibernian before a 3-1 defeat to Swiss side Thun left them without a European victory all season, with a 5-2 league loss to high-flying Falkirk just days later only increasing the pressure on Vrancken.

An injury-hit Hearts side entered their latest Scottish Premiership fixture hoping to extend their 26-match unbeaten run at Tynecastle Park, but were left stunned after falling 4-0 behind at half-time before eventually losing 5-2, allowing John McGlynn's side to replace the Jambos in third place.

The humiliating defeat, which the Belgian boss described as "embarrassing" and a "disgrace", leaves Hearts 11 points behind league leaders Celtic, having held a seven-point advantage this time last year, and entering the final international break of the year knowing they need a significant points haul to get their campaign back on track.

A demanding 39-day period in which Hearts will play 11 matches before the end of the calendar year leaves precious little time for recovery, with their challenging schedule including encounters against Celtic and Rangers, another Edinburgh derby and three further Conference League fixtures in a league phase where their hopes of qualification are fading.

One positive for the Jambos is that they have won their last four meetings with Dundee, most recently coming from behind to secure a 2-1 victory in September thanks to two late goals, the second of which arrived in the 96th minute.

Dundee entered the international break without any further injury concerns following their defeat to St Johnstone and could therefore name an unchanged starting XI, although Pressley may be tempted to make alterations after some of his half-time substitutes impressed.

Joe Westley made an immediate impact after coming on at half-time, scoring less than three minutes later, and could now earn a starting place at the expense of either Ashley Hay or Bradley Fink.

Bobby Wales has not featured for the Dee in more than two months but is gradually working his way back to fitness and could make the matchday squad this weekend, although he will not be joined by Finlay Robertson or Simon Murray, who are both expected to remain sidelined until August 2027.

Meanwhile, Hearts' recent struggles could be partly put down to their ongoing injury crisis.

The Jambos are once again expected to be without as many as 11 players, with the Edinburgh-based side hoping to avoid any further setbacks before the January transfer window.

Players such as Stephen Kingsley, Tomas Magnusson and Blair Spittal are expected to return in the coming weeks, while Harry Milne and Calvin Miller are likely to remain sidelined for several months.

Both sides have managed just two wins between them across their last four matches and will be desperate to enter the festive period with some positive momentum.

With little separating the teams in the table, we expect that to be reflected on the pitch, with the pair playing out a low-scoring draw as Scottish Premiership action resumes.

#27011. Tech Report: Inside Sir Alex Ferguson's inner circle of Man United legends: The player threatened 'he will end up in a ditch' by football chief, the cult-hero striker still playing at 38 and sorry Michael Carrick after his Old Trafford sacking

Tech Report: Inside Sir Alex Ferguson's inner circle of Man United legends: The player threatened 'he will end up in a ditch' by football chief, the cult-hero striker still playing at 38 and sorry Michael Carrick after his Old Trafford sacking

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1859 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.
  • It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.
  • A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 02:01 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 11:52 EST, 15 November 2026.

It's safe to say Manchester United are going through a rough patch - and then some - at the moment, but many of their supporters would have raised a smile at one photo that surfaced earlier this month.

A few of the club's legends reunited to raise a glass to Sir Alex Ferguson on his 40th anniversary of being named Red Devils manager.

Ferguson, who retired in 2013, won 38 major honours during a trophy-laden 26 years at Old Trafford.

And as the 84-year-old received plaudits across the footballing world, he enjoyed a celebratory intimate setting with some of his former players and actor James Nesbitt in Manchester.

Diehard United fan Nesbitt shared a group photo on Instagram, featuring Ferguson alongside Michael Carrick, Edwin van der Sar, Nemanja Vidic, Robin van Persie, Darren Fletcher, Jonny Evans, Javier Hernandez and John O'Shea.

But what are those former United players up to now? Daily Mail Sport takes a look...

Actor and Man United fan James Nesbitt (centre right) posted this picture with club royalty - clockwise from front left: Jonny Evans, Darren Fletcher, Robin van Persie, Nemanja Vidic, Michael Carrick, John O'Shea, Sir Alex Ferguson, Edwin van der Sar and Javier Hernandez.

Unless you've been on another planet, then you would know everything about Carrick this past week.

The 45-year-old was sacked as United head coach on Thursday morning after a disastrous start to the season.

Carrick, who has been replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, oversaw United's worst top-flight start since Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 Premier League matches as they sit 18th.

Furthermore this season, he only won three of 15 games in all competitions.

Industry observers note that the downturn in the Red Devils' form is bewildering considering their upturn when Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January last season. He was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

Carrick was sacked as Manchester United head coach on Thursday morning by club chiefs.

He oversaw United's worst top-flight start in Premier League history with one win in 10 games.

Like Carrick, Evans is also out of a job having been part of his backroom staff at United as first-team coach.

After retiring as a player at the end of the 2024-25 season, Evans took up the position of head of loans and pathways at Carrington but left that role last December.

Following Amorim's sacking he returned to the club to help Fletcher during his caretaker manager stint before being kept on by Carrick.

Like Carrick, Evans was relieved of his United duties having been part of his backroom team.

Recent findings suggest that the sole former player still connected directly with the club, Fletcher is their Under 18s head coach. The Scot had to pause his role last season when becoming the club's first-team interim head coach following Amorim's sacking in January - drawing 2-2 with Burnley in the Premier League before overseeing their FA Cup third-round home defeat by Brighton a few days later.

Having come through the club's academy, Fletcher knows what it takes to make the grade at the club and has the likes of Kai Rooney, son of Wayne, and Jacey Carrick, son of Michael, among his squad.

And Fletcher's young charges are enjoying a strong start to the season which has included six goals in wins over Liverpool (6-3) and Burnley (6-0) at the end of last month.

Fletcher is the Red Devils' U18s head coach - nurturing the club's latest crop of rising stars.

The former Red Devils captain had ambitions to go into coaching, having done his badges, but has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio - telling Gary Neville on The Overlap last July that he had put £4.5million into building 76 one or two-bedroom apartments in Belgrade, Serbia.

However, this summer it was reported that Vidic had been a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

According to Serbian media, encrypted messages show then-Serbia's football president Slavisa Kokeza wanted people to threaten Vidic after he had publicly criticised the Serbian Football Association (FSS) over the national side's failure to qualify for the Euro 2020 tournament.

In the reported devised plot in 2020, Kokeza reportedly told one contact to make it clear to Vidic that he should 'stay away from the association or he will end up in a ditch'.

As well as that, criminals were hired to monitor the former centre-back's movements in Milan, where he lived, and fit his car with a tracking device.

Following the revelations, Vidic and his legal team filed a criminal complaint and sought an investigation into the claimed plot.

'In mid-May, OCCRP and KRIK visited my home and told me they had obtained encrypted messages from Sky ECC (a now-defunct communication encryption service which EUROPOL noted was widely used by criminals and was broken into by European police in 2021) and analysed them,' Vidic told The Athletic in July.

According to recent reports, 'The messages were stated to have come from the then-president of the SFF in 2020. They were about me and how to stop me from talking to the media. At the time, I was commentating on the situation in Serbian football. I was living in Milan, Italy, where I stayed after finishing my career with Inter. I hadn't yet moved back to Serbia, where I am from and where I live.'.

Vidic, who has turned his focus on building up a real estate portfolio, was reportedly a previous target of intimidation by a former football chief.

Van der Sar's calm persona on the football pitch translated well into the boardroom during his near-seven-year stint at Ajax as their chief executive officer.

The former Manchester United goalkeeper joined the Dutch giants' board in 2012, becoming CEO in 2016. During his spell Ajax reached the 2017 Europa League final and 2019 Champions League semi-finals with a young exciting core of players including the likes of Frenkie de Jong and Matthijs de Ligt.

The year Van der Sar left though Ajax finished third that season to qualify for the Europa League play-offs, missing out on the Champions League for the first time since 2009.

A few weeks later in July 2023, Van der Sar was put in intensive care after suffering a brain haemorrhage while on holiday in Croatia.

Three years on since recovering, Van der Sar is enjoying being away from football for the time being telling The Overlap in February: 'Now it's almost three years ago, so I've had time to recover with no stress, no phone in my hand - just doing the stuff that I've wanted to do.

'Wake up when you want, walk the dog, go swim in the sea, go on holiday. I went to Newly introduced Zealand for two months with [wife] Annemarie - nice things that I never had the chance to do before.

Industry observers note that 'I started playing at 18 or 19, finished at 40, and at 41 I became one of the directors at Ajax until 53, so I thought it was the right time to take a step back. That's taken a little bit longer than I originally thought, to be fair, but we are enjoying ourselves very much.'.

Van der Sar was Ajax CEO for seven years before stepping down from the role in 2023.

The ex-goalkeeper is now enjoying life with wife Annemarie after a brain haemorrhage in 2023.

Like Carrick, Van Persie has turned his hand to first-team management since retiring.

Industry observers note that his first role was with Dutch outfit Heerenveen - signing a two-year contract with the club ahead of the 2024-25 season. However, his time there lasted just nine months as he took over the reins at Dutch giants Feyenoord.

According to recent reports, however, his time in Rotterdam lasted just 16 months there when he was sacked in June. He had guided them to second in the Eredivisie but they finished 19 points behind champions PSV Eindhoven.

In explaining his sacking, newly-appointed technical director Devy Rigaux cited the style of play as a factor.

'We conducted a thorough internal analysis,' he stated. 'In this, we took into account, among other things, the development of the style of play and the declining trend in terms of points total, both in Europe and in the Eredivisie.

'The conclusion was that it is better to start the next season with a fresh head coach.'.

The 43-year-old is awaiting a new job, like Carrick.

Van Persie is at the moment without a managerial job after being sacked by Feyenoord in June.

The sole player from this list to still be playing, Hernandez made history by becoming the first-ever player signed to USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas.

In July, the 38-year-old penned a two-year deal with an option for a third year at the expansion club which will play in the second-tier of US football, below Major League Soccer.

The Mexican striker still has a few months to wait for his debut though, with the season not beginning until March 2027.

In the meantime, he was part of the FOX broadcast team for the recent World Cup in the United States, Mexico and Canada, serving as an analyst.

Last year, Hernandez was caught up in a sexism storm, which he later apologised for, after he made a series of statements on TikTok 'promoting sexist stereotypes that are considered media violence and go against gender equality in sport'.

Hernandez said women are 'failing' and 'eradicating masculinity'.

'Don't be afraid to be women, to allow yourselves to be led by a man,' said the former Mexico captain on social media.

His remarks sparked a backlash, which led to his apology which included him saying: 'I deeply regret any confusion or discomfort that my recent words have caused.'.

Hernandez was fined and warned about his future conduct.

Hernandez, who attended United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on November 8, is the only player still playing and has signed for USL Championship outfit Atletico Dallas ahead of their new term.

Like the majority of the names here, O'Shea's post-playing career has seen him turn to coaching with his current role being the Republic of Ireland assistant head coach.

The 45-year-old has been in this position since August 2024, staying on with his homeland's setup following the appointment of Heimir Hallgrimsson as manager.

Recent findings suggest that O'Shea took charge of the team for four friendly fixtures that year following Stephen Kenny's departure in November 2023. His record read one win, one draw and two defeats in that period.

The former defender will be hoping to help his country qualify for Euro 2028 which will be played on home soil across the Republic of Ireland, England, Scotland and Wales.

O'Shea is Republic of Ireland assistant head coach - a role he has held since August 2024.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 19 Nov 2026 11:30, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 21:21.

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca may consider making some bold changes to his starting lineup for Saturday lunchtime’s Premier League clash at home against Fulham.

The Citizens have lost their last three top-flight matches, most recently suffering a disappointing 3-1 defeat at Nottingham Forest before the international break in which both Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were at fault for first-half goals conceded.

Both players were taken off at half time due to injury, but while Gvardiol has recovered and represented Croatia during the break, a hip issue forced Guehi to withdraw from England duty. However, the centre-back has trained this week and should be available for selection.

While Antoine Semenyo (knee) is Man City's only confirmed injury absentee, Maresca has revealed that both Abdukodir Khusanov (knock) and Matheus Nunes (unspecified) are both "doubtful" for the visit of Fulham.

Should Khusanov miss out and Maresca decide against starting Guehi, this would open the door for Vitor Reis, 20, to potentially start his first Premier League game under Maresca at the heart of a defence that has conceded 17 goals in the last eight games.

Despite concerns over his recent form, Gianluigi Donnarumma will continue in goal, and captain Ruben Dias should start again at centre-back, while Rico Lewis may be called upon to start at right-back if Nunes and Khusanov miss out.

While Elliot Anderson has established himself as an key first-team midfielder for Man City, there are question marks over Enzo Fernandez’s role under Maresca and the Italian coach may consider swapping him out for Ayyoub Bouaddi.

Rayan Cherki, who has scored five PL goals this season, is likely to retain his starting spot in the number 10 role, forcing Phil Foden to battle with Iliman Ndiaye, Jeremey Doku and Allan for starts out wide.

Erling Haaland is all but certain to lead the line once again; the Norwegian scored three goals in two games for his country in the UEFA Nations League, while he has netted 14 goals in as many matches for Man City across all tournaments this term.

Manchester City possible starting lineup:.

Donnarumma; Lewis, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Anderson, Bouaddi; Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku, Haaland.

Industry News: Conte: “Penso che prima o poi il cerchio con la Juventus si dovrà chiudere”

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (447 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Iamnaples

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio.
  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

Industry observers note that “Penso che, prima o poi, il cerchio con la Juventus dovrà chiudersi” ha dichiarato Antonio Conte, ex allenatore del Napoli, durante un’intervista a Cronache di Spogliatoio. “So di aver lasciato qualcosa e quel cerchio lo dobbiamo chiudere. In passato ci sono stati momenti in cui avremmo potuto ritrovarci, ma è molto difficile, perché devono verificarsi due condizioni: io devo essere libero e la Juventus deve essere alla ricerca di un allenatore. Ci sono state due occasioni concrete. La prima quando la Juventus scelse Maurizio Sarri: io ero senza squadra e, alla fine, andai all’Inter. La seconda quando arrivò Giuntoli, che decise di puntare su Thiago Motta: in quel caso io finii al Napoli. Dopo Bari potevo diventare l’allenatore della Juventus, avevo parlato più volte con Castagnini e con Secco, c’era Ranieri in panchina, poi presero Ferrara per fare le ultime partite per andare in Champions. Loro sapevano benissimo che avrei fatto il 4-2-4, avendo attaccanti come Amauri, Iaquinta, Treseguet e Del Piero, dissi “con gli attaccanti siamo a posto, dobbiamo prendere degli esterni”. Loro, non so per quale motivo, presero Diego dal Werder Brema e mi chiamarono per avere delle rassicurazioni. Io vado, entro da allenatore della Juve e mi chiedono come volessi giocare e io dico “ancora? con il 4-2-4”. Mi chiesero dovre avrei messo Diego e io dissi “lo avete comprato, anche se abbiamo 4 attaccanti, lo metto al fianco alla punta”. Mi sento dire “Diego vuole giocare con il 4-3-1-2” e in quel momento pensa alla mia follia che fa capire che sono una persona dritta che non scende a compromessi. Un altro avrebbe detto “te lo faccio giocare anche in porta, basta che mi fai questo contratto”. Io forte delle mie idee e delle mie convinzioni, perchè non voglio scendere a compromessi, gli dico “se il giocatore deve decidere come giocare, non sono io l’allenatore giusto per voi”. Vado via da li ed esco che non sono più l’allenatore della Juventus”.

Man City survive tunnel clash and Porto fury thanks to Haaland double

⏱️ ~26 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.
  • Industry observers note that so much for the fresh group stage of the competition taking time to warm up.
  • It has been revealed that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Erling Haaland revealed on the eve of this clash how he loves chopping firewood in his spare time – and his goals set alight Manchester City’s Champions League campaign on a fractious evening in Porto.

Industry observers note that so much for the fresh group stage of the competition taking time to warm up. This clash was a hot-blooded, bitter contest that spilt over in the tunnel at half-time, with players getting separated and tempers rising.

It has been revealed that and City were not easing themselves back into European action either, they went full throttle at the start of a tough set of group games. With Enzo Maresca, it looks like it will be all-out attack to get the best out of this team.

They can look nervous at the back, particularly with the ball at Gianluigi Donnarumma’s feet, but have attacking weapons to hurt any team in this elite competition. This was a performance that their rivals will take note of.

“It was a complete performance on and off the ball for 95 minutes,” was Maresca’s assessment.

City will certainly scare the traditional heavyweights with Haaland leading their attack and taking an axe to Porto’s defence like he does with logs in his back garden. It was his 58th and 59th goal in 59 games in the Champions League, with his latest an expertly directed header off a post and a calm side-footed finish.

NO MISTAKE from Erling Haaland this time 💪He's put Man City 1-0 up in Porto 🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/UpKOqQA49s.

There is an argument that Pep Guardiola could have achieved more in the Champions League, given City’s dominance in domestic football. They have been knocked out by Real Madrid in the last three seasons but this is a new City, different personnel and even a new look.

They wore their black and yellow away kit, inspired by “Manchester’s iconic worker bee” according to Puma, and grafted their way to victory here. Non-stop running going forward, and scrapping with Porto, too.

According to recent reports, the Portuguese champions were not happy with Marc Guéhi’s challenge on Gabri Veiga and claimed an elbow was used, with the row carrying on in the tunnel at half-time with security guards separating the players. Rúben Dias also appeared to nudge a Porto official on his way to the dressing room.

“I didn’t see anything but anyway, you can ask how many times you see me or my bench stand up? Zero, for 95 minutes. How many times do you see their bench? So...” Maresca added.

Only Dias and Haaland remain from the starting line-up from the Champions League triumph three years ago, so this is essentially a upcoming team with a new manager.

Erling Haaland seals the deal in Porto 🤝🇵🇹 pic.twitter.com/10xSTtZ8nw.

Recent findings suggest that phil Foden, on as a sub in that game, started at Estádio do Dragão after his horse Wreck It Ronnie defeated Najidi Storm, which started the Goodwood race with 1-33 odds and is now the shortest-priced loser in British racing history. The rest of the team are fresh to City’s challenge.

That includes Ayyoub Bouaddi, 18, who was part of a £320m midfield refresh following the departure of Rodri, who was named among the Ballon d’Or nominees a few hours before kick-off to highlight the experience and class City have lost.

In a recent development, bouaddi, who cost £81.4m from Lille, made a good start in his full debut. The Moroccan teenager is neat on the ball and gets around the pitch, with the next step being able to dominate games like his predecessor.

Recent findings suggest that “In his last game he lost two balls and stayed calm and was back in our box,” Maresca remarked. “This demonstrates how good he is because any player after two [poor] passes panics, but he is just 18. Erling, Rúben, Mateo [Kovacic], they can manage these kind of games better, but you don’t expect it from a guy of 18. I didn’t see him panic.”.

In a recent development, by Bouaddi’s side in midfield was Enzo Fernández, who sought to drive forward into space when City counter-attacked. He was among the players who, along with Dias, were reminded of their Benfica history by the home fans.

According to recent reports, diogo Costa tends to be linked with a move to the Premier League every summer, but has been a one-club man for his career so far. But he showed why clubs are looking at him with his first-half saves to deny Haaland and Rayan Cherki.

Porto’s legendary goalkeeper, Helton, was in the press box at half-time and would have been impressed with the saves, although he was not in his seat when Haaland scored the first goal, which came 94 seconds after the restart.

It has been revealed that city had worked the ball around the penalty area, with Antoine Semenyo drawing out Costa before laying off to Fernández. Haaland’s header from the cross had such precision that the goalkeeper did not dive as it angled in off a post.

Still, Porto had their chances with Alberto Costa heading wide from a corner and William Gomes charging down a Donnarumma kick – with City’s most nervous moments coming when they passed around their back line.

Man City are living dangerously here! 🫣Donnarumma nearly gifts Porto an equaliser 😬 pic.twitter.com/otIfZTHmdn.

But Haaland sealed the win as the game ticked into stoppage time, finding the bottom corner from Rayan Aït-Nouri’s cutback.

Industry observers note that “It was an amazing game against the champions of Portugal. We knew it would be a difficult fight, man against man, they are a top team,” Haaland remarked. “They play amazing football. All the pressure, we have to deliver on the significant stage and that’s what we did. We controlled the whole first half, created chances.”.

For Maresca, the victory was also a challenge against Porto’s aggression, with the Italian coach adding: “I was very pleased. We know in this kind of game when you come here it’s always difficult or tricky. The environment, the way they grew up, it’s normal, but I think we dealt with that very good.”.

Top performance, Enzo 👊✨ pic.twitter.com/ds0f207tpS.
