📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A Storie di Calcio, trasmissione della radio di Tuttomercatoweb.com condotta da Marco Piccari, protagonista è Andrea Agostinelli. Entrato nelle giovanili della Lazio, ha debuttato in Serie A il 19 ottobre 1975, in Perugia-Lazio (2-0). Nelle stagioni successive guadagna sempre più spazio, ereditando il ruolo di mezzala da Re Cecconi dopo la morte di quest'ultimo, e guadagnandosi la stima dell'allenatore Luís Vinício. Con i romani disputa 75 presenze con 2 gol in campionato, e nel 1979, dopo quattro stagioni in maglia biancoceleste, viene acquistato in prestito dal Napoli. Rientrato alla Lazio, viene nuovamente girato in prestito alla Pistoiese, neopromossa in Serie A, per passare poi per piazze come Modena, Atalanta, Avellino, Lecce e Genoa. Ha chiuso poi la sua carriera da calciatore nel 1992 alla Lodigiani, per poi intraprendere quella da mister. Nella stagione 2002-2003, Agostinelli esordisce in Serie A allenando il Piacenza, poi nelle due stagioni successive allena Napoli e Crotone, entrambe in Serie B.

Recent findings suggest that per Agostinelli purtroppo anche la tragedia, nell'agosto del 2014, della perdita di suo figlio Gianmarco di 33 anni. E su questa storia ha pubblicato il libro "Lo fanno tutti", scritto con Stefano Discreti e Claudio Moretti, che ripercorre la sua carriera, intrecciandola con il profondo dolore privato per la scomparsa del figlio: "Si parla della mia vita calcistica, ma anche di qualcosa di più importante come la morte di mio figlio - ha detto -. Non è naturale perdere un figlio, è la cosa più drammatica che possa accadere. L'ho fatto per far capire a tante persone che si può cadere nel più profondo sconforto ma poi si deve reagire. Mi sono rialzato sempre dalle delusioni, ma qui racconto anche i sensi di colpa di un genitore, che ci sono in questi casi".

Sources indicate that E sulla vicenda ha aggiunto: Sono passati già 12 anni e il dolore non passa mai, ma lo gestisci, che è diverso. Il lutto viene metabolizzato in maniera diversa. Mi ha aiutato il mio lavoro. Inconsciamente sono partito per l'estero e non sono più tornato in Italia, magari per scappare dal dolore. E sono stato un po' egoista, lasciando mia moglie qui. Il senso di colpa è rimasto. Magari se l'ultima volta che l'ho visto lo avessi riportato a Roma, se fossi stato più presente, magari sarebbe stato diverso. Ma magari non sarebbe stato così. Mi ricordo che aveva 22 anni quando mi disse del suo problema, rimasi scioccato. Da quel momento è iniziato il travaglio della famiglia. Ma il lavoro mi ha aiutato tanto. Quando ho scoperto il problema, cosa è successo? Abbiamo fatto di tutto per aiutarlo, siamo andati anche in comunità. Era un amicone, forse la troppa bontà d'animo ha fatto sì che venissero fuori certe problematiche. Ed ecco che arrivano i sensi di colpa. Certe domande me le faccio ancora. E' avvenuto poi a Montecatini, nel posto dove ho avuto le mie soddisfazioni più importanti. Ma questa è la vita. Il lavoro mi ha aiutato ma anche gli amici. Tanti amici, tra cui Bruno Giordano, che è stato uno di quelli più presenti. Credo che la tragedia di un figlio per un genitore sia tremenda".

Anche il figlio ha provato la carriera da calciatore: "Io allenavo la rappresentativa del Lazio dell'81, lui giocava nel Tor Tre Teste ed era uno dei migliori e non lo convocai perché avrebbero detto qualcosa. Poi lui andò alla Primavera del Napoli, alla Pistoiese, e ha esordito in C2 al Fiorenzuola. Forse poi più avanti iniziarono i problemi. Poi tornò a Roma, giocando con i dilettanti, ma era un talento. Non so dove sarebbe potuto arrivare senza il suo problema".

E poi Agostinelli ha anche voluto raccontare un episodio particolare vissuto: "Mi ricordo quando allenai il Partizan Tirana, con i tifosi che dedicarono una coreografia a mio figlio. Ma anche i tifosi dell'Atalanta. Sono cose che ti restano poi. Ricordi di mio figlio? Quando firmai per la Ternana e quel giorno vidi la Primavera della Pistoiese che vinceva dopo 20' con due gol suoi. Mi ricordo le emozioni dentro, come se avessi fatto gol io. Oggi mi dicono che ho il debole per il nipotino, perché più vai avanti e più torni ad avere certi sentimenti".

It has been revealed that sulla sua carriera, invece il mister ha portato alla luce un paio di episodi particolari: "Quando mi chiamò la Juve in segreto e potevo diventare il tecnico, nel 2000-2001. Passò però il treno, ma l'emozione fu incredibile. Volavo in quel momento, uscì poi la notizia su Tuttosport ma lo dissi solo in famiglia. Ci sono dei momenti in cui uno sta per arrivare a un sogno e poi allena anche i ragazzini del quartiere. Ma questo fa parte dell'amore per questo sport. Quello meno bello? Da allenatore ne ho avute, ma anche grandi soddisfazioni. Ma mi ricordo di uno spareggio a Pescara per venire in Serie B. Perdemmo lo spareggio bis, allora il mio tecnico era Mazzone. Vedere i tifosi del Lecce piangere mi colpì molto".

Sevilla have a record of five wins, three draws and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 18 points leaving them in sixth position in the La Liga table.

Los Nervionenses have not managed to finish fourth in Spain's top flight since 2021-22, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a difficult few seasons for the club, finishing 12th, 14th, 17th and 13th in their last four campaigns.

However, Sevilla are presently showing form that could see them claim a European finish, which would be a major step forward given their recent troubles.

The White and Reds have won 61, lost 39 and drawn 35 of their previous 135 matches against Real Betis in all competitions, with their last success over their Seville rivals coming at home in October 2024.

Real Betis have claimed seven points from the last three league matches against Sevilla, including a 2-0 victory at Estadio Ramon last season, while they have lost just once to their rivals since February 2022.

Manuel Pellegrini's side recorded a 2-0 win over Elche in their last league match on November 8, before beating Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey four days later.

El Glorioso have won eight, drawn two and lost two of their 12 league matches this season to collect 26 points, which has left them in fourth spot in the division, eight points ahead of Sevilla leading into this weekend's Seville derby.

It has been a busy opening few months of the season for Real Betis given that Pellegrini's team are also playing in the Champions League; a strong start to their league stage has left them 11th in the table, claiming nine points from four matches.

But ahead of the final group match in St Gallen tomorrow evening, the manager acknowledged it’s incumbent on him to accelerate that time frame.

Sebastien Pocognoli  notes his Scotland team need to show progress 'game after game'.

‘I can tell you that in the time we have had together the players have been doing well in terms of replicating what I ask them to do,’ the manager stressed.

‘They know that and that’s the most important part.

‘They buy in. They like it. I think they enjoy it too. You can see when players don’t enjoy it.

‘For sure, when you win it’s more enjoyable, but it would be very bad if they weren’t enjoying it and we were also not winning games.

It has been revealed that ‘So, right now I think we are working well. We give special attention to the collective.

It has been revealed that ‘In all the camps, I am very clear about what I expect on the pitch. The players wanted this when I arrived. They wanted clarity. And I think that’s what I have tried to bring.’.

To claim second place in the group, Scotland need to defeat the Swiss and hope that Slovenia don’t win in North Macedonia.

That outcome would ensure that Pocognoli’s men would be a pot two side in next month’s Euro 2028 draw.

Asked what it would take to pull off what would be a stunning win in St Gallen, the manager mentioned: ‘Let’s be brave, but be intelligent.

‘It’s about mentality. They (Switzerland) are a very good team, so we need to be smart. Sometimes they will go through our lines with a low block or a high block as they have the quality.

‘We will try to be intense and strong in the duel because I think that’s the first piece to have a good game.’.

John McGinn suggested that it could take 18 months for Scotland to click under Pocognoli.

‘I know we are colleagues, but I’m not reading the press.

‘So, I’m not aware of the criticism. I just want to make the supporters happy.

‘If they aren’t yet happy, we will try to do better.

‘There’s pressure in all the jobs with a club. It can be external, it can be internal. It is part of the job.

‘I’m very self-critical about myself. So, that’s the first thing. Try to be stable when we win, when we lose.

‘I’m always thinking what we can do better. If there’s some criticism, that’s fine.

By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 13:23.

The next instalment of the Borussen derby takes place at Borussia Park when Borussia Dortmund travel to face Borussia Monchengladbach in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

Dortmund come into the clash in second place with 21 points, trailing league-leaders Bayern Munich due to goal difference, whereas the hosts are last in 18th place with just four points.

Gladbach's situation is precarious but not irrecoverable, with the club's tally of four points five fewer than 15th-placed FC Koln, who are the first team outside of the relegation zone.

Head coach Alexander Blessin has only overseen six games as boss, winning twice and losing on three occasions, but his team have taken four points from the last nine on offer in the Bundesliga.

Their latest result was a 3-1 loss against Hamburger SV on November 6, though they did win two and drawn one of their prior three fixtures.

Die Fohlen may ranks as the division's worst defensive team having conceded 25 goals in nine games, but their return of 12 goals in the final third is the second best total in the bottom six.

While Gladbach were defeated in their first three home matches of 2026-27, they have since won once and settled for a stalemate once at Borussia Park, though they are still winless at the ground in the league this season (W0, D1, L3).

Dortmund could find themselves trailing Bayern by three points by the time they face Gladbach due to the fact the Bavarians play against FC Koln on Friday.

Niko Kovac will be delighted by his side's start to the campaign considering 21 points is their joint best tally after nine matchweeks in 13 seasons.

BVB's most recent result was a 2-1 success against Elversberg on November 7, and that was their fifth triumph in six contests.

The club scored at least two goals in five of those fixtures, and though they only managed to keep one clean sheet in that time, no club has conceded fewer goals in the Bundesliga (seven).

Black and Yellow were beaten 1-0 in the corresponding meeting in 2025-26, losing 1-0 at Borussia Park in May, but they emerged victorious in five of their previous six encounters with Gladbach.

Dortmund have taken eight points from a possible 12 on the road in the Bundesliga this term, while they have lost one, drawn two and won just one of their last four outings away from home in all competitions.

As for Dortmund, there are still doubts about the availability of centre-forward Serhou Guirassy, who could have to settle for a place on the bench in favour of Fabio Silva.

Jobe Bellingham and Felix Nmecha have often featured together, and they are the most likely duo to start together in a double pivot.

Emre Can is closing in on a return from a cruciate ligament injury, but he is not ready to play on Saturday, so perhaps fans will see a three-man defence consisting of Joane Gadou, Waldemar Anton and Nico Schlotterbeck.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Quanto mi hanno dato fastidio le fake news attorno a questo?
  • According to recent reports, I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

In a recent development, A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio è intervenuto Raffaele De Leonardis (sindaco di Qualiano): “Quali sono i progetti da affiancare al centro sportivo del Napoli? Dopo la firma ho già pensato a cosa fare attorno alla zona. Quella sarà una cittadella dello sport, perché affianco ai terreni dove sorgerà il centro sportivo c’è uno stadio, ci sono campi da tennis e abbiamo in animo un palazzetto dello sport e una piscina. Oggi c’è la parte più difficile, quella della burocrazia e infrastrutture. In poco tempo che mi rimane come sindaco mi metterò a disposizione. Quante volte è saltata la trattativa con il Napoli e perché? La prima volta è saltata per il prezzo d’acquisto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis doveva valutare l’investimento. I primi terreni con destinazione urbanistica si parlava di 100 euro a metro quadro. Non c’era bisogno della Zes. Servivano 20 milioni di euro. Non era nelle disponibilità e intenzioni della società. Perché poi bisognava costruire il centro. E comparando con il Viola Park, finanziato dal 20% del Coni, ci fu un primo stop. Successivamente, la Zes paventava di superare vincoli urbanistici, allora si è cominciato a parlare di terreni agricoli. E quindi si è riallacciato il rapporto perché c’erano terreni che rientravano nei desideri della SSC Napoli. C’è stata una visita, sotto la pioggia, il famoso 30 marzo dell’anno dello Scudetto. Il Presidente del Napoli mi invitò allo stadio Maradona, vidi Massimo Boldi, c’era Serena Brancale, c’era De Martino. Quanti vaffa mi sono preso dal Presidente? Abbastanza (sorride ndr). Nell’ultima riunione c’era Chiavelli, c’erano Testa, Discepolo, c’era anche Edo e lì ho capito che forse c’eravamo. Se De Laurentiis si è messo in auto per vedere le distanze dalle stazioni ai terreni? Sì, la prima volta che venne a visitare i terreni prima di Napoli-Milan fece questo percorso in auto. Il Presidente De Laurentiis chiedeva quanto distasse dalla stazione di Afragola, ed erano circa 20 minuti, dalla stazione di Ponte Riccio al centro sono 10 minuti a piedi e da Varcaturo o zone residenziali dei giocatori sono 8 minuti di auto e dallo stadio sono 20 minuti con la tangenziale. Dall’aeroporto ancora meno, 12-13 minuti. De Laurentiis percepiva che la posizione era buona. Fece però un passo indietro in merito alla storia dei rifiuti tossici, si era spaventato, ma non era vero.

Quanto mi hanno dato fastidio le fake news attorno a questo? No, sono il Sindaco di Qualiano, ne sento tante. Però penso che ci sono solo pensieri in negativo. Ma pensiamo anche in positivo. Tutte queste problematiche potrebbero nascere, magari con la Zes. Ma noi che ci guadagniamo? Niente! C’è uno strumento di legge, sono stati fatti i migliori investimenti, noi stiamo sperando che non venga approvato? De Laurentiis ha firmato un atto notarile, un preliminare condizionato e se arriva l’autorizzazione, si trasforma automaticamente in definitivo. Lui che se ne fa di un terreno agricolo!? La Zes ha sette linee guida. Una delle linee riguarda l’attività produttiva per quanto riguarda turismo e sport. Noi non ci opporremo, perché sarebbe da folli. Chiederemo le infrastrutture che dovranno essere realizzate e aiuteremo il Napoli a realizzarle. Noi stiamo rispettando la legge. Se il prof Discepolo presenta il progetto definitivo in 10-15 giorni e partono i 90 giorni della Zes, seguiremo il countdown. Sentivo parlare di un’autorizzazione preliminare per il muro di cinta, con autorizzazione dei proprietari. Se ci sarà un laghetto? Non so se è un vezzo, ma servirà per irrigare i campi. Sarà a mo’ di cisterna. Se ci saranno hotel? Ci saranno sicuramente le stanze per i giocatori. De Laurentiis tiene tanto alla cantera, penso che farà anche un convitto per i giovani”.

Napoli, quanta pressione su Allegri: le novità col Torino, ma è già ultima spiaggia

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, vigilia di lavoro e silenzio per Massimiliano Allegri.
  • Industry observers note that la sosta per le nazionali, come già accaduto nella precedente, ha evidenziato il rendimento diverso di diversi singoli che hanno difficoltà nell'esprimersi nel gioco di Allegri in questi primi mesi..
  • Recuperati Favasuli e Spinazzola che ieri hanno svolto l'intera seduta in gruppo mentre per Neres, invece, appuntamento direttamente col Manchester City.

In a recent development, vigilia di lavoro e silenzio per Massimiliano Allegri. Niente conferenza stampa pre-partita a Castel Volturno, per scelta della società che dovrebbe valere anche per le prossime gare di campionato, e quindi il tecnico del Napoli tornerà a parlare solo dopo la sfida del Maradona contro il Torino, una sorta di ultima spiaggia per le zone alte della classifica. Del resto, il Napoli è così indietro in classifica - decimo, appena a +1 sulla squadra di Abate - che è obbligato a vincere non solo col Torino ma anche le prossime con Sassuolo e Lecce per poi con 9 punti approcciare al Milan solo a quel punto con la speranzella di poter accorciare in chiave Champions. La squadra di Allegri però finora non ha mai mostrato di avere continuità (non ha mai vinto due gare di fila) e tantomeno un gioco o un'identità chiara che possa far ben sperare sul medio-lungo periodo. Per questo anche la gara col Torino racchiude tante insidie e punti di domanda.

Industry observers note that la sosta per le nazionali, come già accaduto nella precedente, ha evidenziato il rendimento diverso di diversi singoli che hanno difficoltà nell'esprimersi nel gioco di Allegri in questi primi mesi.. Hanno brillato più di tutti Kevin De Bruyne e Rasmus Hojlund: il belga, tra i pochi a salvarsi in realtà in maglia azzurra, è tornato dominatore col Belgio seppur tra i rumors per il possibile approdo al Psv già a gennaio. L'attaccante azzurro ha invecw chiuso la Nations League con 6 gol (sotto solo un certo Kane) e con la media di un gol ogni 85' ed ha numeri doppi, se non tripli, anche nel coinvolgimento offensivo (tiri, tiri in porta, occasioni e tocchi in area). Ad Allegri il compito di creare condizioni offensive migliori - e più continue - per valorizzare al meglio il loro talento.

Recuperati Favasuli e Spinazzola che ieri hanno svolto l'intera seduta in gruppo mentre per Neres, invece, appuntamento direttamente col Manchester City. Davanti a Milinkovic-Savic (out Meret, ne avrà per circa due mesi, Contini diventa il dodicesimo) è probabile un 3-4-3 con la linea difensiva composta da Beukema (favorito su Marianucci) con Rrahmani e Rafa Marin. In mediana Politano a destra, Anguissa e McTominay al centro ed a sinistra Olivera, tra gli ultimi a rientrare, se la gioca con Spinazzola. In attacco terzetto con Vergara e Lang alle spalle di Hojlund. Non è da escludere, però, l'impiego di Gilmour per alzare McTominay al posto di Lang in una sorta di 3-4-2-1 con i trequarti più stretti dietro l'ex United.

  • Real Madrid have announced that Aurelien Tchouameni has signed a contraction extension until June 2032.
  • The 26-year-old and Jose Mourinho's men have made a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign, with Los Blancos sitting second place in the La Liga standings, just three points behind arch rivals Barcelona.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 13:37, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 13:38.

Real Madrid have announced that Aurelien Tchouameni has signed a contraction extension until June 2032.

The 26-year-old and Jose Mourinho's men have made a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign, with Los Blancos sitting second place in the La Liga standings, just three points behind arch rivals Barcelona.

Following the final international break of the calendar year, Real Madrid return to action at the Bernabeu on Saturday afternoon, when top-flight regulars Celta Vigo are the visitors in La Liga.

The makeup of Los Blancos' squad has shifted massively over the past few years as a number of latest attacking stars have arrived, including French superstar Kylian Mbappe and England's Jude Bellingham.

With his influence waning, Vinicius Junior has endured a difficult start to the current campaign, with the Brazil international struggling since Real Madrid waved goodbye to German legend Toni Kroos.

Communicating to supporters worldwide on their official website, Real Madrid confirmed some exciting news involving Tchouameni, who has started seven La Liga matches so far in the 2026-27 term.

Los Blancos have confirmed that the 26-year-old has put pen to paper on a bumper contract extension at the Bernabeu, committing his long-term future to the 15-time European champions.

Tchouameni's deal with Real Madrid now expires in June 2032, meaning that the Frenchman could spend a decade at the Spanish giants if he sees out at the length of his recently-agreed terms.

The midfielder joined from Ligue 1 outfit Monaco in the summer of 2022 on a deal running until June 2028, meaning that he was approaching the conclusion of his initial agreement at the club.

Tchouameni started the La Liga victories over Barcelona (2-1), Racing Santander (3-0) and Valencia (3-0) prior to the November international break and should play once again versus Celta Vigo on Saturday.

Racking up over 200 competitive appearances since his 2022 arrival from France, Tchouameni has become part of the furniture at Real Madrid, who are looking to repeat their former glories.

The departure of legendary German Kroos left a massive hole to fill in the middle of the park, and Los Blancos are focused on bringing through the next generation of club heroes under head coach Mourinho.

Tchouameni featured in a staggering 55 matches across all competitions for Real Madrid last season, highlighting his importance to a side who have their work cut out chasing down Barcelona this term.

Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Industry observers note that hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

Recent findings suggest that “It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso remarked: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the matter yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also revealed quality and a threat. The joke is at the moment on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a fresh reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

It has been revealed that “Before the season, I noted to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

According to recent reports, “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he mentioned. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Recent findings suggest that hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

According to recent reports, we had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

There have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

Alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

According to recent reports, hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

In a recent development, that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

Martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

Bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Industry observers note that matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Recent findings suggest that within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Industry observers note that tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Industry observers note that pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

It has been revealed that palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Sources indicate that apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

According to recent reports, that’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

There is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

Industry observers note that 5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472.

A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

Recent findings suggest that an almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 14:04.

Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has reportedly prepared to enter talks over the Old Trafford future of Bruno Fernandes.

The 54-year-old Argentine arrives at the Theatre of Dreams with the Red Devils sitting 18th in the Premier League table after winning just one of their opening 10 top-flight games of 2026-27.

That woeful run was eventually enough to remove Michael Carrick from his post at Man Utd, with the club's hierarchy moving quickly to lure Pochettino away from his duties with the United States on the international scene.

As well as Carrick, wonderkid JJ Gabriel has also departed the Red Devils this month, with the teenage sensation set to sign for European giants Real Madrid despite failing to make a first-team appearance for United.

Looking to avoid an unthinkable relegation this season, Man Utd are plotting significant additions to the playing squad during the January transfer window, with a Greek striker supposedly catching the eye.

According to transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano via Football Transfers, fresh Manchester United head coach Pochettino is set to be immediately involved in major talks at the Theatre of Dreams.

The report states that the Red Devils and captain Fernandes have been locked in discussions over a contract extension for the past five months, with an agreement yet to be reached by the two parties.

The 32-year-old's current deal at Old Trafford expires in June 2027, meaning that the Portuguese playmaker would be able to depart on a free transfer at the conclusion of this season.

It is understood that Man Utd are aiming to avoid that scenario, and now incoming boss Pochettino is set to join talks with the player and the club over the future of the influential attacker.

Fernandes supposedly retains interest from clubs in Italy, Saudi Arabia and Turkey, with Champions League-competing Galatasaray attempting to bring the former Sporting Lisbon man to Istanbul over the summer.

Whilst Manchester United's transfer activity since the exit of Sir Alex Ferguson has come under deserved criticism, there is no doubt that the signing of Fernandes was an excellent move by the fallen English powerhouses.

The 32-year-old has been an almost ever-present in the Red Devils ranks since joining from the Primeira Liga in January 2020, scoring 113 goals across a total of 341 competitive appearances.

Fernandes broke the Premier League assist record last season despite his side's immense struggles, and that theme of shining amid the chaos extends throughout the attacker's time in England.

After scoring against Italy, Moreira spoke to Sky, looking at the team’s performance, playing with Kevin De Bruyne and the feeling of grabbing his first goal for his country, as MilanNews relays.

Industry observers note that “I’m very happy with my first goal for the national team. It was a special moment because my family was there. It’s a day I’ll always remember.”.

Mancini remarked that you deserved to win and that you are a very strong team….

“We have some very strong players up front, like Doku, De Bruyne, but I think that in the end it’s a sport where everyone is needed and we all played a great game.”.

What does it mean to play with a player like De Bruyne?

“De Bruyne is special; it’s a pleasure to have him with us because he sees things that others don’t see, he has a lot of experience and we’re happy to have him in our team.”.

What do you take from this experience with the national team at AC Milan?

“I learned a lot in Italy because it’s a league with a lot of experienced players. Playing for the national team and for AC Milan are two very positive things, and I’m very happy.”.

How do you recover in Europe after a difficult start?

“It’s difficult but we’re working towards this. We have to be prepared and we have players who will help us with this.”.

“I’m on the national team right now, and you’re asking me about Milan?”.

Belgium practically overwhelmed Italy, your current footballing nation. It ended 4-1, but the scoreline could have been eight or nine goals….

  • Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.
  • The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 14:06, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 18:04.

Thomas Frank's first assignment as Crystal Palace boss takes him to Coventry City for Saturday's gameweek 11 encounter at the Coventry Building Society Arena.

The Eagles manager's immediate priority will be lifting the South London side off the bottom of the Premier League table, a position that prompted Pierre Sage's swift departure after 10 top-flight matches.

Palace have spent 14 consecutive seasons in the Premier League, and the capital club's board have taken drastic action to ensure that number becomes 15 at the end of the current campaign.

The Selhurst Park outfit entered the November international break in dire straits after a 3-1 loss to Andoni Iraola's Liverpool, marking their fourth consecutive top-flight defeat following setbacks against rivals Brighton & Hove Albion, Newcastle United and Tottenham Hotspur.

Particularly striking during that run were their struggles in front of goal and defensive frailties, highlighted by an alarming 12-1 aggregate score across those defeats that ultimately cost Sage his job.

Frank's reputation suffered during his spell as Spurs boss last season, but his previous work at Brentford should give the Selhurst Park faithful confidence that a turnaround is possible.

Nonetheless, it remains to be seen whether the Dane has conveyed his ideas in less than a week of training, with the international break also denying him access to his full squad, as the London club seek to end their four-match losing sequence.

A first victory since October and third overall would lift them above this weekend's 17th-placed hosts and potentially out of the bottom three, although the latter outcome depends on results elsewhere.

Coventry's 3-1 defeat at Everton before the pause left Frank Lampard's men alongside Arsenal and Manchester City as the only clubs yet to draw in this season's Premier League campaign.

However, while the defending champions and Man City occupy positions in the top three, Coventry's nine points leave them just one clear of the relegation places heading into a busy period.

Lampard's men can take encouragement from collecting six of those points in front of their adoring supporters, who witnessed October victories of 4-1 over Newcastle and 3-1 against Sunderland either side of a narrow 1-0 defeat to Fulham.

Although the absence of home clean sheets remains concerning, the Sky Blues' seven goals across their last three matches at the Coventry Building Society Arena represent clear progress after they failed to score in opening defeats to Hull City (1-0) and Brighton (5-0).

Now, the West Midlands side aim to secure consecutive home Premier League victories to avoid slipping into the bottom three.

Caleb Yirenkyi and Bobby Thomas (calf) are doubtful for Coventry this weekend, while Luke Woolfenden (knee) and Josh Eccles (ankle) face late fitness tests; however, Frank Onyeka, Aurele Amenda (calf), Haji Wright (thigh) and Ephron Mason-Clark (knee) are expected to miss out.

Jack Rudoni is the only home player to have scored more than once, with the attacking midfielder's three goals accounting for 30% of the Sky Blues' tally of 10 this term.

After registering assists in consecutive appearances against Newcastle and Spurs in October, Brandon Thomas-Asante has dropped to the bench, but the Ghanaian forward will hope to play a pivotal role for Lampard's team this weekend.

One Palace player denied the opportunity to make an immediate impression is Jean-Philippe Mateta, who serves the second game of a three-match suspension following his straight red card in October's 2-0 defeat at Spurs.

Further concerns surround Ismaila Sarr (groin) and Jorgen Strand Larsen (ankle), who are doubtful for this weekend's encounter and could leave Frank without several match-winners.

While former Arsenal defender Takehiro Tomiyasu (calf) is also touch-and-go for Saturday's match, Chadi Riad's knee injury will keep him sidelined until 2027.

Rushworth; Van Ewijk, Mfuni, Pinnock, Dasilva; Torp, Grimes; Sakamoto, Rudoni, Gboho; Awoniyi.

Crystal Palace possible starting lineup:.
